features.gist: prior BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy is linked to poorer later checkpoint results
features.note: Prior BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy has been associated with poorer results from later checkpoint blockade; in the DREAMseq trial, starting with combination checkpoint blockade gave longer overall survival than starting with BRAF/MEK inhibitors.

features.gist: lung-only spread carries a better prognosis than other visceral spread
features.note: In AJCC eighth-edition staging, distant spread limited to the lung carries a better prognosis than other visceral or brain disease, and under pembrolizumab the absence of metastases beyond soft tissue and lung was associated with longer survival.
features.direction: relatively favourable compared with other visceral sites

features.gist: a higher metastatic stage means greater disease extent and worse prognosis
features.note: A higher AJCC M category, meaning visceral or brain spread, reflects greater disease extent and worse prognosis; it is prognostic rather than a validated predictor of anti-PD-1 response.

features.gist: a larger checkpoint benefit reported in men is debated
features.note: A meta-analysis reported a larger relative benefit from checkpoint inhibitors in men than in women, but the finding is debated and sex is not an established predictor of response.
features.direction: uncertain; a possible modest male advantage

features.gist: how the tissue was sampled, not tumour biology
features.note: This records how the tissue was sampled, surgical resection versus core biopsy, not tumour biology; in the foundation study the only misclassified patient was a core biopsy with few immune-rich tiles, so sampling can affect tissue-based scores.

features.gist: elevated lactate dehydrogenase is an adverse prognostic factor
features.note: Elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase is an established adverse prognostic factor in metastatic melanoma, is part of AJCC M staging, and was associated with shorter survival under pembrolizumab.

features.gist: prior ipilimumab does not exclude response to anti-PD-1 therapy
features.note: Anti-PD-1 therapy remains active after progression on ipilimumab in randomised trials of pembrolizumab and nivolumab, so prior anti-CTLA-4 exposure does not exclude response.
CD8+ iNOS+ cells were more frequent in responder tiles in the foundation study, where iNOS expression in cytotoxic T cells was among the features associated with anti-PD-1 response.
features.direction: leans responder in the foundation cohort

features.note: PD-L1+ and CD8+ cells were most frequent in the immunoreactive responders of the foundation study, but PD-L1 positivity alone did not separate responders from non-responders, and CD3+CD8+PD-L1+ cells clustered together more in non-responder tiles.

Responders in the foundation study showed stronger co-occurrence of CD8+ T cells with PD-L1+ and LAG-3+ cells, and earlier work linked CD8+ T cells and PD-1/PD-L1 contacts at the invasive tumour margin to anti-PD-1 response.

In the foundation study, CD3+CD20+ cells were more frequent in non-responder tiles and B- and T-cell markers co-occurred more strongly in non-responders, possibly reflecting a suppressive B-cell role without tertiary lymphoid structures; elsewhere, B cells organised in tertiary lymphoid structures were associated with checkpoint response.
features.direction: leans non-responder in the foundation cohort; context-dependent elsewhere

features.note: In the foundation study, iNOS+ cells and iNOS+ melanoma cells were more frequent in responder tiles, but nitric oxide has both anti- and pro-tumour roles and some iNOS+ clustering patterns were greater in non-responders.
features.direction: mixed, leaning responder in the foundation cohort

features.note: nNOS was measured to study the dual role of nitric oxide in melanoma; the foundation study did not report nNOS+ melanoma cells as a standalone predictor of response.

A sampling-site covariate rather than tissue biology; the foundation study listed varied collection sites as a limitation, and distant visceral disease, particularly in the liver, has been associated with reduced anti-PD-1 benefit.

Cytotoxic T-cell density at the invasive tumour margin was associated with response to pembrolizumab, and in the foundation study CD8+ clustering was greater in responder tiles and models restricted to CD8-rich tiles performed best.
PD-L1 expression is an imperfect biomarker: PD-L1 positivity alone did not separate responders from non-responders in the foundation study, and responses occur in PD-L1-low tumours.
